text:
sophie: Quick question — PR #4123 proposes allowing hosted spillover for Dedicated customers on the STANDARD tier when a tenant's dedicated pool is saturated. Before I iterate the console mock, want to align on contract/telemetry/route semantics.

dan: saw the PR, skimmed. The code change is smallish (routing hook) but the policy surface is bigger. link: https://git/repo/pull/4123 :eyes:

alex: my 2c: enterprise customers with Dedicated paid contracts expect zero hosted touching. We should NOT enable spillover by default for enterprise. For standard/trial we can consider. Also we need an explicit opt-in flag per-tenant, not a global fallback.

maria: telemetry/observability items: if we allow spillover we must tag requests with routed_reason="spillover_hosted" and record original_tenant_plan masked for PII. Metric suggestions: routed_spillover_count_by_tier, spillover_rate_by_region, spillover_latency_ms histogram. Also add an audit log entry per spillover.

samir: infra note: we can implement two behaviors: (A) fallback to "hosted_same_model_variant" (try to use exact model version on hosted pool) or (B) fallback to "hosted_compatible_variant" (quantized/cheaper variant). Option B is cheaper but changes tokenization/behavior. Need opt-in per-tenant for B. Also KV cache won't help across dedicated->hosted so we lose prefix cache and see latency bump.

sophie: good points. Contracts/legal: enterprise = no spillover. For STANDARD I propose default = opt-in (tenant must enable). That avoids surprising customers. Thoughts?

ux-anna: UX: surface a per-tenant "Failover policy" in Console with three radial options: Strict (reject when Dedicated unavailable), Hosted same-model (best-effort hosted fallback), Hosted compatible (allow cheaper hosted variant). Tooltip: "Strict = preserves dedicated isolation; Hosted options may use hosted infra and affect data residency." Add a small banner showing last spillover time and count.

maria: telemetry: add alert rule: if spillover_rate > 1% sustained for 5m for a single tenant, page SRE. Also tag cost_impact per-spillover so billing and cost dashboards can show unit economics.

dan: from API perspective, add tenant config key: `fallback_policy` with enum ["none","hosted_same_model","hosted_compatible"], and `spillover_enabled` boolean for quick toggle. Route decisions should consult tenant policy + region preference + model allowlist.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: canary plan appended to rollout doc: will enable for 10 internal standard tenants in us-west first, monitor spillover_rate and latency.

deploy-bot: CI failing on PR tests: integration test needs sim of placement table with no dedicated capacity. I'll queue a fix.

alex: safety: ensure hosted fallback honors tenant's allowed-models list (no private/custom models should leak to hosted). Also enforce region affinity: do not send EU-restricted data to us-hosted endpoints. If no matching region variant available, respect tenant policy (fail vs allow degraded region).

samir: implementation detail: routing engine needs tenant_policy as part of the routing key. We can keep placement table semantics but add a `spillover_capacity` boolean and an eviction circuit-breaker that gradually throttles spillover to avoid flash-cost. Also need to add a profiler flag to measure KV cache miss penalty.

sophie: summary action items: (1) I'll update PR text with the `fallback_policy` enum and default to `none` for enterprise and `none` for standard unless opt-in is set. (2) UX mock from @ux-anna and tooltip copy. (3) @maria telemetry metrics/alerts + audit log spec. (4) @samir infra changes for routing key and circuit-breaker. (5) add API contract in Platform API docs.

alex: vote: opt-in default for standard.

maria: +1 opt-in.

dan: +1 opt-in.

ux-anna: +1. I'll draft the console screens.

sophie: ok setting default opt-in=false in the PR and adding canary plan. tagging legal for sign-off on wording on console and billing.

ops-bot: Canary plan scheduled: will enable for 10 tenants at 2027-08-01T17:00Z in us-west-2. Monitoring dashboards: infra/spillover (added by @maria).

deploy-bot: CI green after fix, merging to canary branch once legal ok.

sophie: thanks everyone — I'll push the updated PR and add TODOs in the issue for post-canary review (billing delta, customer comms).
